chunks: And by this same chain of narrators — from Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Umar ibn Udhayna, from Zurara:

He said: 'I performed wudu one day without washing my private parts, then I prayed. I then asked Abu 'Abdullah (peace be upon him) about this, and he said: "Wash your private parts and repeat your prayer."'

key_terms.أَعِدْ: repeat/redo (imperative); the jurisprudential ruling commanding invalidation and repetition of the prayer
key_terms.ذَكَرِي: my private parts (male organ); washing it after urination is required as istinja' for a valid wudu

ai.seo_question: Is washing the private parts (dhakr) obligatory before wudu in Shia fiqh, and must the prayer be repeated if this step was omitted?
ai.summary: Zurara narrates that he once performed wudu without washing his private parts (dhakr), then offered prayer; when he consulted Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), the Imam ruled that he must wash his private parts and repeat his prayer. This hadith is a foundational proof-text in Shia fiqh establishing that washing the private parts as part of istinja' after urination is a prerequisite for the validity of wudu and prayer.
